text: The 1956 Summer Olympics, officially known as the Games of the XVI Olympiad and branded as Melbourne 1956, were held in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, from 22 November to 8 December 1956, with the equestrian events taking place in Stockholm, Sweden, from 10 June to 17 June 1956. These were the first Olympics held in the Southern Hemisphere and Oceania, marking the first time the Games were staged outside Europe and North America, and Melbourne became the most southerly city ever to host the Olympics. Due to the seasonal differences between the hemispheres, the Games were held during the warmer spring/summer in Australia, corresponding to the Northern Hemisphere's autumn/winter, making them the only summer Olympics ever held in November and December. Australia hosted the Games for a second time in 2000 in Sydney and will host again in 2032 in Brisbane. The equestrian events were held in Stockholm because of Australia's strict equine quarantine regulations, making it the second time the Olympics were not held entirely in one country, following the 1920 Games in Antwerp with events in Amsterdam. Despite concerns from the IOC about Melbourne's southern location and the unusual timing, which was thought to inconvenience Northern Hemisphere athletes, the Games proceeded successfully and were known as the "Friendly Games." Nine nations boycotted the event: Egypt, Iraq, Cambodia, and Lebanon in response to the Suez Crisis, and the Netherlands, Spain, Liechtenstein, and Switzerland in protest of the Soviet invasion of Hungary; the People's Republic of China boycotted due to a dispute with the Republic of China over representation. Athletes from East and West Germany competed together as the United Team of Germany. A total of 67 nations participated, with eight making their Olympic debut—Cambodia (only in Stockholm), Ethiopia, Fiji, Kenya, Liberia, Malaya, North Borneo (modern-day Sabah), and Uganda—while nations like Afghanistan and Colombia returned. The Games featured 17 sports, 23 disciplines, and 151 medal events (145 in Melbourne and 6 in Stockholm). Australia won the most medals, and the Soviet Union won the most gold and overall medals. Notable events included a controversial water polo match between the Soviet Union and Hungary, which ended in a cancellation after violence and injuries, with Hungary declared the winner due to being in the lead; a major upset in the 3,000-metre steeplechase where Chris Brasher of Great Britain was initially disqualified but later awarded gold after a reversal; and the debut of the "Parade of Athletes" at the closing ceremony, conceived by John Ian Wing, a Melburnian, which became an Olympic tradition. The Olympic flame was relayed from Olympia to Athens, then transferred to a miner's lamp flown by a Qantas Super Constellation to Darwin, then transported by a Royal Australian Air Force Canberra jet to Cairns, where it was lit on 9 November 1956 by Mayor W.J. Fulton. The flame was then carried down Australia’s east coast by runners using die-cast aluminium torches, arriving in Melbourne on 22 November, where it was lit by Ron Clarke, who accidentally burned his arm. While international television rights were not awarded, domestic rights were granted to GTV9, HSV7, and ABV2 in Melbourne, with Sydney stations syndicating the coverage; television in Australia was new, and around five thousand sets existed, with broadcasts viewed in community halls and petrol stations. The Melbourne Olympic Arts Festival was held in conjunction with the Games. Betty Cuthbert won gold in the 100 and 200 metres and the final leg of the 4×100 metre relay, earning her the nickname "Golden Girl"; Shirley Strickland won the 80-metre hurdles and was part of the winning relay, amassing seven career Olympic medals. Australia dominated swimming, winning all freestyle events and earning eight gold, four silver, and two bronze medals; Murray Rose became the first male swimmer since Johnny Weissmuller to win two freestyle events and a total of three, while Dawn Fraser won gold in the 100-metre freestyle and as lead-off in the 4×100 metre relay. The United States dominated men's track and field, winning 15 of 24 events, including sweeping four and finishing first or second in five others; Bobby Morrow won gold in the 100 and 200 metres and the 4×100 metre relay, and Tom Courtney narrowly beat Great Britain’s Derek Johnson in the 800-metre race before collapsing and requiring medical attention. Ireland’s Ronnie Delany won the 1,500-metre run with a time of 53.8 seconds over the last 400 metres, securing Ireland’s last track gold; Mildred McDaniel set a high jump record of 1.76 metres, and Egil Danielsen threw a javelin of 85.71 metres. Hungarian athletes were widely cheered, and Laszlo Papp won a record third gold in boxing. A publicized romance between American hammer thrower Hal Connolly and Czechoslovak discus thrower Olga Fikotová led to her representing the United States after the Czechoslovak Committee refused to allow her to compete for Czechoslovakia; she competed in every Olympics until 1972 and was flag bearer for the U.S. at the 1972 Games. The India men's field hockey team won its sixth consecutive Olympic gold. The India men's field hockey team won its sixth consecutive Olympic gold. John Ian Wing was awarded a bronze medal for his idea of the "Parade of Athletes." The Republic of China effectively represented only Taiwan. Five nations competed in the Stockholm equestrian events but did not attend Melbourne: Cambodia, Egypt, and Lebanon due to the Suez Crisis boycott, and the Netherlands, Spain, and Switzerland due to the Hungarian invasion boycott. Nations that had participated in Helsinki 1952 but were absent in Melbourne included the People's Republic of China, Liechtenstein, Netherlands Antilles, and Saar, with Saar joining West Germany in 1957. Puerto Rico, the Bahamas, Bermuda, Fiji, Gold Coast (modern-day Ghana), Hong Kong, Jamaica, Kenya, Nigeria, Malaya, North Borneo, Singapore, Trinidad and Tobago, Uganda, and British Guyana were all part of the British Empire. The top ten nations by medal count included the host nation, Australia.
